headline: High-risk orchestration pair: Kestra can write and egress broadly while LlamaFactory is read-only, making prompt-injection and leakage low, but cascading misuse and compliance gaps remain possible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kestra can emit workflow outputs over stdin/stdout, files, Slack, email, and other channels, while LlamaFactory has no clipboard/MCP/files surfaces and no direct ingestion channel is documented. A prompt-injection bridge is therefore not default, but if operators manually copy Kestra-generated text into LlamaFactory prompts, the pathway exists with small blast radius.
conditions: IF operators manually paste Kestra output into LlamaFactory prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared message queue or file bridge is added between them, the risk increases.
mitigations: Disable manual copy-paste between agents.
Route Kestra outputs through a structured schema, not free text.
Add a human review step before any LlamaFactory prompt ingestion.
Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, inputs, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, but LlamaFactory has no filesystem read, no network egress, and no declared data classes. With no shared workspace or outbound channel on B, leakage from A into B is limited unless operators explicitly move files or text across.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem or manual file transfer is introduced, Kestra data can reach LlamaFactory.
IF LlamaFactory is wrapped by another service that uploads prompts externally, leakage risk rises.
mitigations: Keep separate storage locations for each agent.
Do not pass Kestra artifacts into LlamaFactory prompts.
Restrict Kestra outputs to redacted summaries.
Audit any wrapper service around LlamaFactory.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kestra can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while LlamaFactory cannot write files, modify git, or use MCP. There is no overlapping mutable resource in the profiles, so direct write-write conflict is not documented. Uncertainty is low, but if an external orchestrator grants B write access, conflict could emerge.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory, conflict becomes possible.
IF an orchestrator adds shared locks or queues, the conflict is reduced.
mitigations: Keep LlamaFactory read-only.
Separate writable directories per agent.
Avoid shared git worktrees.
Serialize any file-producing Kestra jobs.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra can generate workflow outputs and act on them through APIs, email, Slack, PagerDuty, AWS, and cloud services. LlamaFactory is a model stack that can produce instructions or text, so if Kestra feeds its outputs into LlamaFactory and then acts on the result, errors can cascade across multiple work products. No verification step is documented.
conditions: IF Kestra uses LlamaFactory output as authoritative workflow input, cascading error risk is present.
IF downstream tasks send notifications or execute cloud actions without verification, impact expands.
mitigations: Require human approval before actioning model output.
Add validation rules to Kestra workflow inputs.
Use a second model or rule-based checker for critical steps.
Log and diff model outputs before execution.
requires-engineering: implement confidence-gated task routing.

E_compliance.rationale: Kestra touches logs, inputs, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, which can include regulated data, while LlamaFactory’s profile shows no data classes or outbound channels. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to operator-chosen data flows rather than a default breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed from Kestra into LlamaFactory prompts, compliance review is required.
IF a third-party wrapper around LlamaFactory stores prompts or logs outside policy, retention risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to LlamaFactory.
Redact logs and artifacts before transfer.
Document retention for Kestra outputs.
Review any external wrapper’s data residency.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated fields.
